content_voiceover: This marked must-know table compares prognostic factors in adult versus pediatric ALL, and the boards love testing these age and immunophenotype cutoffs. In adults, age under 35 is favorable while over 60 is adverse; white count under 30 for B-cell disease is good, but over 100 for T-cell disease is bad. Thymic T-ALL is a favorable immunophenotype, whereas early T-cell precursor ALL is adverse. On genotype, there's no strong favorable marker in adults, but BCR-ABL1, MLL-AF4 rearrangement, and hypodiploidy under 44 chromosomes are all adverse, and MRD under 0.01% after induction is the favorable cutoff. In children, the sweet spot age is one to nine years, with under one or over ten being higher risk. B-lymphoblastic immunophenotype is favorable while early T-cell precursor is again adverse. Hyperdiploidy over 50 chromosomes and ETV6-RUNX1 fusion are the classic favorable pediatric markers, while hypodiploidy under 44, MLL-AF4, and IKZF1 alterations are adverse, and pediatric MRD thresholds flag anything over 1% as adverse.
keypoints: Adult favorable: age <35, thymic T-ALL, MRD <0.01%
Pediatric adverse: age <1 or >10, hypodiploidy <44, IKZF1
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the mirrored pattern: extremes of age are bad in both groups, and early T-cell precursor immunophenotype is adverse whether you're looking at kids or adults. Favorable genetics differ by age group, hyperdiploidy and ETV6-RUNX1 in children, while adults lack a strong favorable marker but share the same adverse hits, BCR-ABL1, MLL-AF4, and hypodiploidy under 44 chromosomes.
